title: Console feature onboarding: dashboards, rollout controls, and cost insights — launch coordination and enablement
creator: Alex Kim
description: Coordinated launch plan for three Console UX features shipping together: (1) Per-route cost breakdown dashboard, (2) Canary/A-B rollout controls with traffic shifting, (3) Model-level performance dashboards. Deliverables include release notes, in-product help, enablement sessions for Sales/SE/Support, and an interlock with Engineering for rollout verification and hotfix procedures.
background: These console capabilities were developed to give customers clearer visibility into per-model and per-route economics and safe deployment controls. PM, Design, and Eng decided to ship the features in a single console release to provide a coherent story for cost management and rollout safety. This ticket coordinates marketing, docs, internal training, support runbooks, and release-note sequencing.

release_notes_draft: Headline: New Console insights — understand costs, control rollouts, and track model performance

Summary: Today we’re shipping three console features that help teams reduce inference spend and deploy model updates safely. You can now see per-route token spend, run controlled canary rollouts with traffic shifting, and compare model latency/throughput on per-model dashboards.
- Cost breakdowns: per-route and per-model token costs with timeframe filters and top-N spenders
- Rollout controls: canary groups, traffic split, automatic rollback thresholds, and audit logs
- Performance dashboards: latency P50/P95, request volume, and model-specific variance charts
How to get started: Follow the in-console guided tour or watch the 5-minute walkthrough video linked in the docs.
Important notes for admins: Role-based access controls apply for rollout actions. Consult the admin section of the docs for RBAC configuration.

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customers misinterpret cost numbers and open billing disputes. Mitigation: clearly state cost calculation methodology in docs and include examples.
Risk: Rollout misconfiguration causes broad traffic shift. Mitigation: default canary limits, require two-step confirmation for >20% traffic, and audit log visibility.
Risk: Post-release performance regression. Mitigation: pre-release load test, canary with pilot orgs, and automated rollback thresholds.
